transcript: So you know how every piece moves and captures in the same way? How about this one doesn't? Just so it's a nightmare to explain to kids. It's going to move in a straight line, but only in one direction. I don't like the idea of it moving backwards for some [music] reason. It's going to always move only one square at a time. Except for the first move. I want this to be the weakest piece on the board, basically worthless for the entirety of the game. But then, if it reaches the other side of the board, it completely flips the result. It decides the outcome of the game. Something actually broken like It can become any other piece it wants. On a second thought, you know that thing that I said about taking two steps on the first move? [music] I don't actually like that. How about we create an extremely obscure and complicated rule specifically just to counter that? And the best part? There is going to be as many as all of the other pieces we've created this far combined. So simple, right?
